utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, sir, that the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I start examining the witness, I wish to inform the Trial Chamber that the Viktorija Taseva, legal assistant on the Defence team of Mr. Boskoski, is also present at our hearing this morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. M-039. My name is Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague Mr. Mettraux, I represent Mr. Ljube Boskoski. On behalf of Mr. Boskoski and on behalf of the Defence team, (redacted) (redacted), but, at the same time, I would like to ask you nevertheless to listen to my questions carefully and could you please answer me to the best of your knowledge in view of the facts involved. Did you understand what I said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I would like to ask for a private session, briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On Friday, the 10th of August, 2001, you heard mortar fire from 7.30 until 8.00, as you said in your statements; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: One shell fell close to your house; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The women and children were terrified, so you decided to go to Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And to leave your family there; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although Macedonia had been confronted with terrorist attacks by the KLA for several months by then, Albanians in Skopje were quite safe. So that was the reason why you took your wife and children to Skopje; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You took your own Golf, a yellow Golf; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A yellow colour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today, you have a Golf III, which is red; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although the police stopped you, nevertheless, on that day, sometime after midday you managed to reach Skopje; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 10.00 or 11.00, I arrived in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From a public telephone booth, you called your brother in Ljuboten, and you found out from him that your mother was very upset because she had received information to the effect that you had been killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You left your family in Skopje, and in order to pacify your mother you decided to go back to Ljuboten on your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since the Macedonian citizens were very upset because of the death of the soldiers of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, you did not use the road via Ljubanci; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You took a bus on line number 57, and with that bus you came to the last stop in Radishan; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The penultimate stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, one can reach Ljuboten from Skopje from the south-east, too, that is to say, opposite Ljubanci via Radishan; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this road, you could notice many civilians who were rather upset and, if I can put it, that were rather hostile after this incident with the shell; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Page 6, line 2, it says here after the shelling, but actually I was referring to a mine incident at Ljubotenski Bacila.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel. The interpreters cannot hear her.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon, my microphone was not on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I will repeat my question. In view of the fact that you saw a large number of civilians in the street, you did not dare take the regular road, rather, you decided to walk to the village through the meadows hiding along the way from the local inhabitants; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Mr. M-039, when you came to Ljuboten, did you see your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where your mother was at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that she was in your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, our house. My father's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your mother remained in the house throughout with you; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what time it was when you arrived in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not look at the watch, but it was between 2.00 or 3.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After your arrival in Ljuboten, you found out that one shell had killed a six-year-old boy; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not see the death yourself, but you saw the father carrying the boy; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not my father who was carrying the boy. We heard that the boy was killed by a shell, and from that moment on, we entered our basements and we didn't move.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, perhaps you didn't understand what it was that I said. I thought that you saw the father of the killed boy carrying his killed son. Is that what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see his father. We just heard that this boy was killed by a shell, and we then remained in our houses, didn't move about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your previous statement, you said that you did see the father carrying the dead boy. Then that was probably a mistake, wasn't it, in that statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the night between Friday and Saturday, you were in your father's house and, for the most part, it was a calm night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was rather calm on Saturday, too. There was just sporadic fire; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was sporadic fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now go briefly back into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nearby (redacted) (redacted); is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The new house. His new house is nearby my house, while his old house is a little bit further.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You knew all the sons of (redacted); is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we're in public session, perhaps we should redact this part that refers to their relationship.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On their new house, there is a balcony from which one can see the positions where the army of the Republic of Macedonia was, and it also faces the entrance into the village from the direction of Ljubanci; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To which balcony are you referring?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the balcony on the new house of Aziz Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see anything from there. You can go and check for yourself that you cannot see any of the positions of the Macedonian army. What you're saying is not true. You can't see absolutely anything from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if someone were to say before this Court that he or she could see from that balcony the houses in the area where the families of Jusufi live or that one could see yet another area, that would be incorrect; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see anything from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On Sunday morning, you did not see anyone, any of the sons of Aziz Bajrami that is; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for Xhelal. And I guess you're speaking about Sunday, right?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So as for Mevludin or Nevaip, you didn't see them that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Their new house was much safer. It had a better cellar, and that is why you decided to go to that house; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were joined at the house by Xhelal Bajrami and Sami Jashari; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only by Xhelal Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So to the best of your recollection on that Sunday morning, Xhelal Bajrami, Kadri and Bajram Jashari, you and your father were together; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You remained inside this house until about 13-, 1400 hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. It was afternoon or midday. I can't be very precise about the time. We didn't look at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't even know what was going on in the other parts of the village because during that time, the phones in the village were not working; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No one, from among you, had a mobile phone or had any conversation with other persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said in your statements that when you saw that the police was coming close to the village, you panicked and left the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We left the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Xhelal Bajrami, Kadri and Bajram Jashari did not go with you. They started going upwards, towards the house of Kadri Jashari, Qani -- Qani Jashari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They left for the house of Qani Jashari, and then I didn't see them anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move now back into a private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the place where you hid, you heard shootings, but you could not distinguish whether they were coming from the positions of the army or from the group of Macedonians that was near your houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the moment, they came not from the army but from the Macedonian police. They came to the house of Basa Natovski [phoen]. They fired. They shot at the house. But not the army, the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your previous statement to the Prosecutor, you have stated that there was a haystack near the house, and that this was the first thing set on fire. Am I understanding this well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was, yes, a haystack in front of the house, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The smoke from that haystack made it even more difficult for to you recognise what was happening around the houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you don't know who and when set this haystack on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Macedonian police that did that, because they came there with Hermelin inside the yard. Don't tell me something else from what really happened. They fired from the road. Please don't make me nervous. Don't tell me untrue things. They came with their Hermelin inside the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-039, I'm not disputing your statement about the Hermelin arriving. Probably you have seen it as you have testified. But what I'm asking you is: Is it correct that you personally did not see who and how set the haystack on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the police. Who else could have done that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you personally did not see with your own eyes the moment when someone set the haystack on fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, the 12th of August, 2001, was a true summer day. It was very warm in Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And otherwise the summers in Skopje are very hot. The temperature rises above 40 degrees of Centigrade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That day, it wasn't that hot. It was -- it wasn't more than 20, 25 degrees. It was even a cloudy sky. So don't tell me these things. It wasn't over 20, let's say 25. Indeed, in the afternoon, it even rained.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask to move to into private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After this event where your family suffered such losses, you didn't go to the police to tell your story there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke with international organisations, you gave statements to them, organisations such as OSCE, the International Committee of the Red Cross and the investigators of the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Neither you nor other citizens of Ljuboten wanted to be interviewed by the Macedonian police or cooperate with it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't know how this witness can speak about what all the other citizens of Ljuboten wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would suggest the question should be confined to this witness, Ms. Residovic. He may -- at the moment, he may be able to tell us about others, but you haven't set the ground for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honours. Maybe then we will present the relevant ground to arrive to this question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not agree with the police and the court coming to the city, to the village to make an investigation on the site. You only allowed the OSCE to enter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We allowed them to come, even this gentleman who is sitting behind. He was called on the phone and told to come and see what they -- what they had done to Ljuboten, what massacre they had committed. It was Tuesday when they called him asking him to come and see, so don't tell me lies here. And he knows very well who called him. We waited there for two hours. We didn't bury the bodies of the dead people for two hours waiting for them to come, and they never came. There were people from the OSCE, from the Red Cross, and they saw that we were waiting there for them to come.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 14th of August, 2001, the bodies of the deceased were buried in the clothes in which they were found; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the burial, you yourself did not perform a search on the bodies of the deceased; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't because they were shooting all the time from that position. Once we left the house, they began shooting. How could we do that? We just made sure that the corpses were not eaten by some dogs or some other animals.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In April 2001 -- 2002 - Interpreter's correction - an exhumation of the bodies was performed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, in March 2002, there was a meeting in the village with the representatives of the OSCE and the International Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, the efforts, the attempts of the court in Skopje to perform an exhumation of the bodies were prevented by the villagers of Ljuboten. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. This is a lie. Enver Tahiri was there. We were waiting. So, please, please, don't tell me lies. Enver Tahiri is there, he's alive, he was -- he can tell you we were there gathered at the school, but you refused. You said they are not from Ljuboten, they are from Kosovo. So why are you lying here? Enough with lies, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the meeting that you had with the representatives of the OSCE and the ICTY, you have just mentioned the investigator Howard Tucker. You were there as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is correct. I was there, too. And I have with me the newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the representatives of the other families of the persons killed were present in the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask that the witness is now shown the evidence 1D83 -- which is 1D8 now. Yes, could you please rotate it? Yes, and could you zoom it in a bit, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, zoom it in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under the items 5 and 6, is your name written there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's my understanding that we are in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps we need to go into private session or redact a couple of recent comments.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't see that I have mentioned anything. The documents are not shown to the public as far as -- this is how I understood the Court's decision, and I think that I have never mentioned anything that would disclose the identity of this witness. I just said that he was present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is correct. It's my mistake, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. I was still struggling to see the problem. There isn't one. Carry on, please, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-039, these are the notes of the investigator Howard Tucker. You yourself just mentioned that he was present in the meeting. Apart from you and the other persons whose names you saw on the screen a moment ago, the crisis committee of the village was represented in the meeting by Kenan Saliu, Hisni Sadri, Nadri Musliu?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hisni Versali [as interpreted], and I don't remember the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the fourth paragraph from the top in the English, it says: "Persons representing the crisis committee of Ljuboten are: Kenan Saliu, who is the president of the crisis committee; Hisni Murseli, secretary of the crisis committee; and Nadri Musliu, he is the head of the village of Ljuboten." So if this refreshed your memory about the persons present, could you tell me whether the ICTY investigator described correctly who were the persons representing the village in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. Maybe he was. I know that Hisni was there. The others may have been there, too, but I just don't remember. Maybe they were in their relevant capacities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the bottom of this page, you see that there were the persons representing the OSCE, their names are written here, and the ICTY was represented by Howard Tucker, investigator, and Sydilik that is the operational officer who was stationed at the ICTY office in Skopje. You remember that they were present in the meeting as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the top of the document, it is written that the meeting took place on the 8th of March, 2002, at the school in Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but it was in the school, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask now that the second page of this document is shown, 1D9.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would put it to you, Mr. M-039, I would read the last paragraph where it is stated [In English] by the spokesperson of the crisis committee, Mr. Saliu Kenan, about the involvement of the Republic of Macedonia agency: "Feelings were obviously running high, and there was talk of non-cooperation by the villagers. However, after further discussion, they all agreed their support for the investigation." [Interpretation] Did the investigator correctly describe what you were saying then at the meeting and what was pointed out by your representative, Mr. Saliu Kenan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, I don't know. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could page 3 of this document be displayed now, please, that is of 1D9?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the fourth paragraph from the bottom, you see some words in bold and that is the conclusion of the investigator after this meeting where it says: "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... mistrust of anything Macedonian." [Interpretation] Is it correct that all of you present there displayed this huge mistrust towards everything Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And I still don't trust them and I will never trust them. This is the truth. What they did to us, nobody in the whole world could do. How can I trust him? Tell me, how can I trust him? Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-039, on the 14th of August, 2001, you were present when the persons who had been killed in Ljuboten were buried; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, you came to the village with the representatives of the OSCE; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the OSCE members came to my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, you came from Skopje with the representatives of the OSCE; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say to you, Mr. M-039, that on the 12th you were not in the village but that you came on the 14th; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at home on the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But not on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're saying. Can you please repeat your question? On the 12th of August, I was at home with my brothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have concluded my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Good day, Your Honours. Today I will question the witness, Mr. M-039.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. M-039, My name is Antonio Apostolski. I am the lead counsel for Mr. Johan Tarculovski. With me is my colleague, co-counsel Jasmina Zivkovic. I will ask you questions about the events in village of Ljuboten in the period between 10th and 12th of August, 2001? My learned colleague from the Prosecution presented the basic data about you, where you were born, when, where you live and what was the education that you completed. In 1985, you served the conscription military service in Banja Luka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Which military branch was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tank unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You have training on how to handle infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At 8.00 on the 12th of August, 2001, the shelling of the village started; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move into a private session for a moment, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Since the shelling gained in strength, you decided to look for a new shelter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You went to the house the Xhelal Bajrami; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It was just Xhelal who was in his house when you arrived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stayed at Xhelal's house until 1400 hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Then you heard shooting coming from the house of Adem Ametovski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Which frightened you and then you left the house and went to the house of Bajram Jashari. You left the house of Xhelal Bajrami, I apologise. I apologise again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You and Qani Jashari went a few metres down by the road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only my father did so. I set off in the direction of my house, but I wasn't able to get there, so I remained where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You were running uphill, up the sand road towards the house of Qani Jashari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, towards my house. That's where I wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move into a private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn now then, Mr. Apostolski, and resume again at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness M-039, is that the location where you saw the Hermelin arriving from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me what was the colour of the Hermelin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to put it. I wasn't next to it to look carefully at the colour. I only know that it stopped there and started to fire in the direction of Qani Jashari's house. I wasn't a journalist or an expert to look at it. I could hardly survive, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: After that, you saw three or four bottles being thrown from the location of the Hermelin to the house, and it was set on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The Hermelin entered inside the yard, at the house of Qani Jashari. And then it was when they threw the bottles.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you saw three or four bottles being thrown onto the house, petrol bottles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them hurling the bottles, but I cannot tell you whether they were bottles or bombs. Probably it was petrol, because the house was immediately set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that you did not see with your own eyes the bottles being thrown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While the Hermelin entered the yard, they were throwing these things, and they were shelling and firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: After the house was set on fire, you saw Kadri Jashari, Bajram Jashari and Xhelal Bajrami leaving the house through the window; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But there was a lot of smoke rising from this haystack that was burning. They left from the window, and then I saw them no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So despite the smoke, you saw them leaving the house through the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Then after that, because of the flames and the smoke, I saw them no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So if anyone were to state that first they left the house, and only after that the house was set on fire, then the person would not be speaking the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First the haystack was set on fire, burned the house, and then they left through the window. The house was in the course of being burned. The smoke was rising out of it, and then they left through the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move into private session, briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: After the security forces left, you climbed out of your shelter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, (redacted) (redacted), is that correct, or should it be redacted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will redact it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You couldn't walk to the bodies because fire was coming in your direction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Only after it became dark, you dared go out and find the bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you were questioned by my distinguished colleague from the OTP and when you showed the pictures of the bodies of Kadri Jashari, Bajram Jashari and Xhelal Bajrami, you said that you have written in your own handwriting that the bodies were not moved from the position where they were killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, everything happened as I described it, until Tuesday when they came to bury them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move into private session, briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know Shefajet Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he's a cousin of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that his nickname is Shef?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. His name is Shefajet Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that he is a NLA member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Maybe he is, but I don't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move into a private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know Baki Halimi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Baki Halimi as a fellow villager -- as a teacher. He used to be my history and geography teacher. This is how I know him, as a teacher and a fellow villager.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown a photograph, N005-7605? Could we just zoom in on to the left part of the photograph? Thank you very much. That's it, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the photograph in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark with number 1 the house of Baki Halimi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark with number 2 -- could you mark the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd also like to see marked the house of his father, but I don't know whether it is outside of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Otherwise, please mark with number 2 the house of your father.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark it with number 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we tender this photograph in evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D18, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for the witness, M-039.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we show the exhibit that I believe was marked as 2D17?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, can you take a look at this photograph, please? Slightly above the arrow where we see the letters M39, you made a mark indicating the spot where you saw the Hermelin vehicle on that Sunday, August 12th; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And subsequently, you explained to my learned colleague that you saw the Hermelin vehicle enter the yard of the home of Qani Jashari; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Hermelin first was here, at point number 2, and then it continued upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps with the usher's assistance could I ask you, Witness M-039, to take the pen on the computer, that blue -- perhaps the same blue pen, and draw the route that the Hermelin vehicle took.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Witness -- Witness, I don't think you understood me. I'm very sorry. My question wasn't clear. If you could erase that blue line that you just drew, please. My question should have been: Can you draw the route that the Hermelin vehicle took from that point number 2 up into the yard of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. After that Hermelin vehicle went up -- up that road into the yard of the house, before the time that the house and the haystack caught on fire, did you see anyone else go up that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we tender the photograph as it is now marked, please, as a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you like to have a number 3 in blue against the markings?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That would probably be an asset. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If the witness could be directed to draw the number 3 below the broken line that he has just drawn.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If that could be tendered, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P204, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, if we can move on to another topic briefly. You mentioned to my distinguished colleague that someone had called, I believe, Mr. Boskoski to come to Ljuboten. Can you help us, please, if you know, who called Mr. Boskoski to come to Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that Tuesday, when we were getting ready to bury my brothers, the representatives of the Red Cross and of the OSCE were present, as well as Mr. Fatmir Etemi. He called them to come and confirm that these were civilians who were massacred. They told him, Just wait for us, we'll be there in two hours. Two hours past. Three hours past. They never came. Then Mr. Fatmir Etemi and the Red Cross representatives gave the green light for the burial to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, you say that Fatmir Etemi called them to come and confirm, and then you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know who he spoke with, who precisely he spoke with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know what institution Fatmir Etemi called, if he called an institution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he called the Macedonian institutions to come and verify that those massacred were civilians. This is what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did Fatmir Etemi give you this information, or did you learn it from someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were just nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What -- well, you didn't answer my question. Did Fatmir Etemi tell you about his telephone calls, or did you learn about them from someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-039 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fatmir Etemi was precisely here when he made that phone call. I don't know who he spoke with precisely, but he then turned to us and said, They are not coming to see the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. My learned colleague read to you part of a paragraph from a statement given by --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move into private session briefly, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will be pleased to know, sir, that that completes the questions for you. The Chamber would thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance that you have been able to give, and you may now, of course, return to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours, for presenting us with the opportunity to come here and tell the truth. May you live thousands of years. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, indeed. The court officer will assist you out now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Saxon, the next witness has effectively full protection measures. That requires that we break for 20 minutes to enable the technical equipment to be set up. Given the time, I think the obvious course to take is to have our normal second break now and resume at 25 minutes to 1.00 and then have an hour and ten minutes with the next witness. We will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is now shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Now, Mr. Saxon, has some questions for you. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very sorry, Your Honour, for the confusion. With great respect, the next witness will be led by Ms. Meritxell Regue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Witness. If I could have, please, the usher's assistance in providing the witness with the identification paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please read the document that is being provided to you and let us know whether the information is correct? And please don't read it aloud.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, can you please repeat --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, after my learned friends have seen the document, and if there are no objections, I would like to tender the document. Could that be tendered under seal, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P205, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, you have been granted protective measures of face and voice distortion. Therefore, your face cannot be seen outside this courtroom, neither your real voice can be heard. We will be referring to you as Witness 88 or Witness. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will start providing a brief summary of this witness's evidence. This witness is an ethnic Albanian and resident in Ljuboten. He was a truck driver during the relevant time period of the indictment. Between 10 and 12 August, 2001, the witness heard sporadic gun-fire and shelling in Ljuboten. The witness states that there was no NLA presence in the village during that weekend. He observed how the police entered Ljuboten in the morning of the 12th of August, 2001. And afterwards, houses were set on fire. Also, on Sunday, the 12th, he and his family were informed that police were mistreating people, especially youngsters in the checkpoints, and he and his cousin were the only singles. They were advised to run away and hide somewhere. They decided to go up hill, and for that they had to pass by the Jashari's house. There, they met Xhelal Bajrami, Kadri and Bajram Jashari, who call them inside. He saw no weapons in the house. They left the house when they heard an APC and police outside the courtyard. The witness was under fire when he was running away from the police. Finally, he was able to seek shelter in the woods. After two days, he went to a monastery where NLA people were deployed. He joined the NLA for a short period of time. He was told that the NLA commander had prevented any NLA intervention in Ljuboten during that weekend.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, what I just read is an accurate summary of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. But at the end, when you said that commander in Ljuboten, that was not right. Refer to those in Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. So I will refer to the NLA in Matejce. Matejce monastery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Witness, do you recall providing information to the Office of the Prosecutor on June 2004?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting with a registrar, on August 2006, who certified, put a stamp on your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to read the statement in your native language back then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to introduce corrections?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you introduce any corrections back in 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, I made one correction. In the case of a T-shirt, white, of white colour and light yellow. Green, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Today, do you agree with the correction that you made back in 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What would you like to state instead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I would like to state that in the light green T-shirt, I made a mistake. Because I saw some photos in 2006 shown to me by the OTP investigator, and I had on a kind of purple, dark purple colour T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And what do you think that you made the mistake back in 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Before I made this correction in 2006, I had seen some photographs of the victims of the brothers Kadri and -- Jashari and Xhelal, and I was very sad, and I made this mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to read your statement before coming here to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that the statement that you read was correct and accurate, including the correction that you just indicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, now it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this witness's statement under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Statement bearing ERN N002-7224-1 will be admitted as Exhibit P 206, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we move briefly to private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could I please ask not to display the next photo that I'm going to show to the witness outside this courtroom? And I will call photo N005-7603. For Your Honours and my learned friends, this is the photo depicted in court binder page 5. Thanks. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, what do you see in this photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I see a view of Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. In the prior photo, you just mark and indicate the area where the police enter the village on Sunday morning. Could you please take the pen --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could have the usher's assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: -- and draw a circle in the area where you saw the police entering the village on Sunday, the 12th? If you can see that in the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, it is this area here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please write number 1 there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall something extraordinary happening after the police enter the village that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, in this part, there was smoke.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you also draw a circle there and write number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. It is this part here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Does this area of Ljuboten has any particular name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. It's called Mahalla e Nazallareve.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you know any family living in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, Jusufi family lives there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, I would actually like if we could move the photo a bit to the right? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We lose the image, that is the markings, if we move. So it may be necessary to -- if there is nothing more to be marked on this photo, to receive this photo and then move the image.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We can do that. Sorry, I would like to tender with the markings, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P208, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could I have displayed the same ERN -- the same photo again, without markings? Thanks. Could I move briefly into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to see the house of your relative in the photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we move the photo a bit to the right, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And now, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please take again the magic pen and draw a circle in the house of your uncle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, now we have sort of lost a bit the picture, but we saw that there is an important distance between this house and the area where you saw the police entering the village. How come you were able to see the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: From here, it's on the same aerial plane. That's why I could see the police, and they were wearing black uniforms, uniforms in dark colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P209, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I like to call 65 ter 199.22. For Your Honours and my learned friends, it is page 9 of the court binder, photo A. And it's okay if we display the photo outside this courtroom. That is no problem. If we could have 65 ter 199.2 -- sorry, it's coming up. Thanks. This is okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What does it show?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: It shows part of the village, another part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you know the name of this part of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. Mahalla of Nazallareve -- standing for neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Based on your prior evidence, is this the neighbourhood that you saw the smoke coming out after the police enter the village on Sunday, the 12th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, this is the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And also based on your prior evidence, is this the neighbourhood where the Jusufis are living or were living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. This is the Mahalla where Jusufi family live.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you able to see the Jusufis' house in this photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please, if we take the pen, and if you could please draw a circle around the house of Rami Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, this is the part. The entire family lived here, or lives here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you able to identify which is the house of Rami Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. It must be here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P210, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to call 65 ter document 199.15. It's the page 12, photo B of the court binder. This is not the right photo, actually. The ERN is N004-4698.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 199.15, 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. It seems to be a mistake between the correlation. We have a hard copy to place on the ELMO, if there is a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph you've given reference is 65 ter 199.10.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us what do you see in this photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. I see Qani Jashari's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were you at this house at any time on the weekend of 10 to 12 of August 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, I was, on the 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: With whom were you in this house?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I stayed for some five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you have to leave the house at some point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Because I heard a noise coming from the street. It was the noise of an armoured car, and then I left. There were shots and insults in Macedonian, and then I was obliged to leave this house.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: How did you leave the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I left through the window.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And where did you go afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I went up to the place where there was tobacco.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sorry, we can see, actually, in the house two windows. Which window did you use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: The place which is kind of on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. After reaching the tobacco field, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I stayed there for a while, a little while. I saw two or three policemen and the armoured car. The policemen were wearing black uniforms and wearing black masks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And what did you do afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Then I left this place, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I went to the forest.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You just mentioned that you saw two policemen. From the noise that you heard, did you think that there were two policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I saw them with my own eyes from the tobacco field.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: But, Witness, my question is: From the noise, did you think there were two policemen only?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No, from the noise, they were more. But I managed to see only two or three.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, please, could you please take the pen again, if I could have the usher's assistance, and if you could draw a circle in the window where you jump off and write number 1, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: This is the window here, number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you also please draw a circle in the tobacco field where you hided and write number 2, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, it is this place here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And could you please indicate with a cross the place where you saw the APC and write number 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. It is this place here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P211, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could I have, please, 65 ter 199.12, bearing ERN N004-4842? It's the photo depicted in the page 12 of the court binder, photo D. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What does it show?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: The house of Qani Jashari, and the window from which I left.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And well, in order to speed up --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, could you also take the pen - sorry - and draw a circle in the window and mark it with number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. It is this here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And also a circle in the tobacco field and write number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: This is the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please draw a line indicating the route that you took when you ran away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: This is the route.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please write number 3 in the forest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P212, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Finally, Your Honours, could I have 65 ter 615? Sorry, we won't be needing that pen anymore. Thanks. This is not the photo, actually. We have a hard copy as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise what is depicted in this photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you describe it, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. This depicts the tobacco field, the location where I spent a short time. And above, you can see the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Does this tobacco field looks like when you were there in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. It looked like this exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P213, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. M-088. I am Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague, Mr. Guenael Mettraux, I defend Mr. Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a citizen of Macedonia, you were aware of what happened in Kosovo, especially during the time of the open conflict between the Albanian population and the Yugoslav army; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: If you could repeat your question, because I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. Thank you. I'll put it in simpler terms. You, like all other citizens of Macedonia, followed what was going on in Kosovo at the time when the Albanian people of Kosovo fought against the Yugoslav Army, and when NATO had to take measures in order to protect the Albanian people in Kosovo. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. From the way that I see the formulation of the question, my learned colleague mentioned the Albanian people of Kosovo. This is quite a boarder term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what your point of concern it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours -- well, from my understanding from the question, it seems that all the Albanian population of Kosovo took part in the fight. And I'm not sure whether this is quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It clearly isn't, but I don't think it was meant to be. It's a general description of a conflict in which, on the one hand, there were the Albanian people of Kosovo, and, on the other hand, there was the Yugoslav Army. I don't think it's too misleading. Have I got your understanding correctly, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that you understood me well. I believe that the witness understood me, too. Because it wasn't only in Macedonia, but throughout the former Yugoslavia people follow what was going on with attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know about what was going on, Mr. M-088?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, as a citizen of Macedonia, you knew that in that year, 1999, the Republic of Macedonia took in over 300.000 Albanians from Kosovo who were expelled from their homes. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But I'm not here to testify about the refugees who fled Kosova. I'm here to testify about the 2001 event that occurred in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-088, I would kindly ask you to answer every one of my questions that you can. Since you previously answered my question, I'm sure that you knew that at that time the Republic of Macedonia and its authorities were given ample recognition by the international community and the Albanian population of Kosovo for the efforts made by Macedonia to take in the refugees from Kosovo. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, in the Republic of Macedonia, various extremists and terrorist groups of Albanians started attacks against police stations, police patrols and the civilian population. As a citizen of Macedonia, did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Not far away from your village is Aracinovo, where Albanian groups attacked the authorities and the people who lived there, and this was one of the first attacks that took place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a citizen of Macedonia, I'm sure that you know that from March until the month of July, thousands of Macedonians were expelled from their homes in the areas where these terrorist groups were operating. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I thought we are in private session; I thought we weren't. A few moments ago, you said that as a truck driver, you crossed the border with Kosovo almost every day. I'm sure that as you crossed the border in the areas of Kumanovo and Tetovo, you could notice intensive conflicts in which these terrorist groups were attacking the areas of Kumanovo and Tetovo. Could you see that? Could you notice that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I did not cross the border from Kumanovo and Tetovo area. I transported the watermelons from Strumnica, and I usually crossed at the Blace border crossing, not at Kumanovo or Tetovo border crossings.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sorry, I think we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we are in open session. That's what I understood Ms. Residovic to understand in the end. She was not certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that what the witness has been saying so far could not jeopardise his identity in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, sometimes you'd cross the border near Stenkovac; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, it is near Blace border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You did not go to the closer border crossings precisely because of these attacks and the very difficult security situation in the area; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No, that's not right. This is not true. Because I did not have to use that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-088, at the time, did you learn of information provided by KFOR from Kosovo, indicating that various terrorist groups were crossing the border and smuggling weapons into Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Do you expect me to answer this question?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Did you have such information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe we will go back to the questions that you are able to answer, because you have certain knowledge of that. Your village, Ljuboten, is on the slopes of Skopska Crna Gore; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of its position on these slopes, it dominates the Skopje valley; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes. It is actually in the Skopje valley. On the area of Skopska Crna Gore.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of its geographic location, you will certainly agree with me if I say it has an exceptionally important strategic significance for the defence of the city of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. Can you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ljuboten, because of its specific geographic location, was of exceptional strategic importance for the defence of the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the importance was even more significant because the old mountain road above Ljuboten, known among the people as Sultan's or Murat's Road, connected the areas of Kumanovo, the area of Kumanovo and the border to Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No, I have never heard of this road.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you surely know that two or three months before the events in August, the army of the Republic of Macedonia expanded the area of control of border to the depth of 20 kilometres and stationed its positions also in the area around the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But could you, Mr. M-088, agree with me, that Ljuboten was important also for the members of the NLA, since it was in the vicinity of Skopje, and since it was important as a logistics base or support for the forces in the regions of Kumanovo and Matejce?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with you on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me now, do you know that, as early as in the time of the first attacks of NLA against the governmental forces, so to say, in Aracinovo, some young men from Ljuboten actively joined the units of NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No, I don't know if Ljuboten people participated in Aracin?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is, do you know that immediately after the events in Aracinovo, a number of young people from Ljuboten joined NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes, for some of them, I could say that they were, but not in Aracin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know a person by the name of Zendeli Islam. Do not say if you have any personal relationship with him, just say whether you know him or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If he were to say that he personally joined NLA before the attack in Aracinovo, you would agree that he were a member of the NLA from Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask now that the witness is shown 65 ter number 1D94, page 1D1316, item 2, Macedonian 1D1323, also item 2. I would like to ask the court that the documents shown to this witness are not published to the general public.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-088, is this the data of the person that we just discussed, Zendeli Islam, a son of Ifran, is that the person that I asked you about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I would like to ask that the page 1D1316.2, while Macedonian is 1D1323. No, I apologise. 1317.2. Let me see if I give you the correct number of the Macedonian page. Again, .2. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see here in item 2 that Islam Zendeli says that he joined NLA three or four days before the Macedonian forces performed the offensive to Aracinovo, and that was one or two months before the events in Ljuboten, in June 2001? Is this statement of Islam reminding you that he, as a villager of Ljuboten, was a NLA member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: At that time, he was living in Skopje, and as I worked as a driver, I was not aware of his whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I would like to ask that the witness is shown page 1D1318, paragraph 14; while the Macedonian is 1D1325, again paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In his statement given to the investigators of the ICTY, Islam Zendeli, as you can see written in this item, in this paragraph in last sentence, he said that there were other people, maybe 25, 27, from Ljuboten, in the ranks of NLA. He further then said when the event in Ljuboten took place, they were in the area of Kumanovo. My question is: Do you know that, in August 2001, there were at least 25 to 27 NLA members from the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088
utterances.text: No. I could not say that, because I don't know if there were that many. So maybe it's better for him to explain his statement. Personally I cannot say if there were 25 or 27 men from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think this is a convenient time, Ms. Residovic. We must now finish for the day. Sir, we have to stop our proceedings at this time. We resume again tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15, and if you could return in time for that. We will adjourn now.
